div.head: IV Eg 11
div.ab: Gif he þonne cynne, þæt he hit mid gewitnesse bohte, ⁊ þæt leas bið, sy he þeof ⁊ þolige heafdes ⁊ ealles þæs þe he áge; ⁊ healde se landhlaford þæt forstolone orf ⁊ þæs orfes ceapgyld, oð þæt se ágenfrigea þæt geacsige ⁊ mid gewitnesse him þæt orf geahnige.

Gyf he þonne cænne, þæt he hit mid gewitnysse bohte, ⁊ þæt leas bið, sy he þeof ⁊ ðolige heafdes ⁊ ealles ðæs þe he age; ⁊ healde se landhlaford þæt forstolene orf ⁊ ðæs orfes ceapgyld, oð þæt se agenfrige áð geacsige ⁊ mid gewitnesse him þæt orf geahnige.

At si demum necessitate compulsus, aliquem supra dictorum testificatur, idque fore falsum reperitur adque dinoscitur, mortis reus affectus, sine dilatione capitali sententia puniatur, et in uerticem ipsius iniquitas eius conuertatur. Furtum igitur illud sub potestate domini rus supradictum habentis transeat, quoadusque possessor, cui fuerat hóc ablatum tali fraude, ultroneus adueniat, sibique illa uendicando quod suum est, cum iurisiurandi sacramento recipiat.

Gyf he þonne cænne þæt he hit mid gewitnysse bohte, ⁊ þæt leas bið, sy he þeof ⁊ ðolige heafdes ⁊ ealles ðæs þe he age; ⁊ healde se landhlaford þæt forstolene orf ⁊ ðæs orfes ceapgyld, oð þæt se agenfrigea þæt geacsige ⁊ mid gewitnesse him þæt orf geahnige.

Dagegen wenn er erklärt [hat], dass er es unter Zeugenschaft gekauft habe, dies aber falsch ist, so sei er ein Dieb und verwirke den Kopf und alles, was er besitzt; und es bewahre der Grund- [und Gerichts]herr das gestohlene Vieh und den Werth des Viehs [als Busse für den Bestohlenen], bis dass der Eigenthümer dies erkundet und durch Zeugenschaft das Vieh sich zu eigen erklärt.

But if he has declared that he bought it with witness, and that is false, let him be a thief and forfeit his head and everything he owns; and let the landlord [and lord of the court] keep the stolen cattle and the value of the cattle [as compensation for the person robbed], until the owner finds out about it and claims the cattle as his own with witness.

If, however, he makes it known that he has bought it in the presence of witnesses, and that statement proves false, he shall be regarded as a thief, and shall forfeit his head and all that he possesses; and the lord of the manor shall keep the stolen livestock, or its equivalent value, till the owner hears of it, and proves his claim to the livestock with the help of witnesses.

If, however, he declares that he bought it with witness, and that is false, he is to be regarded as a thief and to lose his head and all that he owns. And the lord of the estate is to keep the stolen cattle or the value of the stolen cattle, until the owner discovers it and proves his right to the cattle with witness.
div.note: C's ‘að’ (from ‘þæt’ misread; the Versio also has ‘sacramento’) should be corrected from F. Liebermann cites Psalm 7.17 for the Versio's ‘in uerticem ipsius iniquitas eius’.; BF: added from Gesetze I p. 212, October 2026 (MS C (Latin)); O: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Latin version of C)”, now “∅ (moved to BF)”)

also Versio sacramento; correct from F [-a þ was misread as aþ]

Die Entkräftung der Behauptung legitimen Erwerbs, also ein blosses Indizium, genügt zum Beweise des Diebstahls, aus welchem das Todesurteil folgt (vgl. von Bar Beweisurteil 38), wie bei erfolgreichem Anefang (s. d. Gl 17) der Gewährbruch

The refutation of the assertion of lawful acquisition, thus a mere piece of circumstantial evidence, suffices as proof of theft, from which the death sentence follows (cf. von Bar Beweisurteil 38), as does failure of warranty when the attachment (see that word in Gl 17) succeeds

Das Vieh, dessen Erwerb nur lügnerisch als rechtmässig behauptet war, gilt als ertappter Diebstahl, daher sein Besitzer als handhaft (s. d. Gl 3) und friedlos (s. d. Gl 10b); Enthauptung (s. d. Gl 2) allein braucht, laut Versio, nicht mit Schmid 656 verstanden zu werden, sondern auch andere Todesstrafe. Und praktisch trat wohl oft nur Verstümmelung ein; s. zu I Atr 1, 6

The cattle, whose acquisition had only falsely been claimed as lawful, count as theft caught in the act, and their possessor therefore as taken red-handed (see that word in Gl 3) and outlaw (see that word in Gl 10b); according to the Versio, beheading (see that word in Gl 2) alone need not be understood, with Schmid 656, but other forms of capital punishment too. And in practice probably often only mutilation took place; see on I Atr 1, 6

Ich halte II S. vii die frühere Übs. für falsch und verstehe mit Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 164: ‘das Vieh, bzw. [wenn es unterging] den Wert des Viehs’. Denn ceapgild kann nicht æftergild (II Cn 24, 1) synonym sein, und die Busse fällt wie Hu 2, 1 fort, da den Täter Friedlosigkeit (s. d. Gl 13) traf. Stellen, wo and (s. d. Wb) ‘oder’ heisst, sind auch Abt 9. 87. Ine 73. 74. VI As 1, 4

In II p. vii I declare the earlier transl. wrong and, with Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 164, understand: ‘the cattle, or [if it has perished] the value of the cattle’. For ceapgild cannot be synonymous with æftergild (II Cn 24, 1), and the compensation lapses, as in Hu 2, 1, since the offender incurred outlawry (see that word in Gl 13). Passages where and (see that word in Wb) means ‘or’ are also Abt 9. 87. Ine 73. 74. VI As 1, 4
Der Herr verwahrt den einzuklagenden Wert dem Eigentümer auch sonst; vgl. Gerichtsbarkeit 11d
Elsewhere too the lord keeps the value to be claimed in safe custody for the owner; cf. Gerichtsbarkeit 11d
Versio übs. den Fehler að in C
The Versio translates the error að in C

Probably and is used here, as frequently, with the sense of ‘or,’ cf. I Edm. 3; III Atr. 1, 1. If the livestock has been killed its value is to be set aside from the thief’s property and given to the rightful owner (see Liebermann, iii. p. 143).
